scope: Primary methodological sources for task-relative summary sufficiency, finite receiver determinacy, provenance-preserving repair, and equivalent plain comparison.
execution_policy: Read-only primary-source review; no implementation, browser study, deployment, recruitment, or human-participant claims.

primary_sources.title: Views and Queries: Determinacy and Rewriting
primary_sources.publisher: ACM SIGACT-SIGMOD-SIGART Symposium on Principles of Database Systems (PODS)
primary_sources.source_type: peer-reviewed conference paper; publisher DOI and author-hosted full paper
claims_used: A view determines a query when the view information uniquely determines the query answer.
Determinacy and rewriting are relative to the declared view/query and data model.
A finite same-summary/different-receiver pair is a direct counterexample to determinacy on the frozen world set.
primary_sources.gate11_use: Define receiver-specific conditional adequacy over finite fictional worlds; test each receiver independently.
primary_sources.limits: Formal database result; finite instrument checks do not establish universal determinacy or human understanding.

primary_sources.title: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance
primary_sources.publisher: International Conference on Database Theory (ICDT), Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science 1973
primary_sources.source_type: peer-reviewed conference paper; publisher DOI and institutional author copy
claims_used: Why-provenance identifies source data that contributed to an output.
Where-provenance identifies source locations from which output data were taken.
primary_sources.gate11_use: Require source record/field and derivation pointers for summary and repair fields; treat provenance as origin evidence, not a newly inferred fact.
primary_sources.limits: Provenance characterizations require a specified data/query setting and do not evaluate explanation quality or human interpretation.

primary_sources.title: Provenance Semirings
primary_sources.publisher: ACM SIGACT-SIGMOD-SIGART Symposium on Principles of Database Systems (PODS)
primary_sources.source_type: peer-reviewed conference paper; publisher DOI and author-hosted paper
claims_used: Symbolic semiring annotations track provenance and alternative derivations through relational computations.
The framework covers incomplete, probabilistic, and bag-semantics settings.
primary_sources.gate11_use: Carry stable derivation/source identifiers through the equivalent plain comparator and any allowed minimal repair.
primary_sources.limits: Annotations record formal derivations; they do not justify adding unsupported values or establish semantic understanding.

derived_gate11_requirements.design: Freeze worlds, summary, and receiver functions; require equal summaries to imply equal receiver answers across the frozen world set, and retain same-summary/different-answer counterexamples.
Declare an allowed field menu in advance; expose only an existing allowed dependency or source pointer, preserve its origin/derivation, and add no inferred fact.
derived_gate11_requirements.basis: Buneman, Khanna, and Tan (2001); Green, Karvounarakis, and Tannen (2007)

derived_gate11_requirements.design: Use the same records, formulas, fields, provenance identifiers, and repair state in both representations; do not treat visual agreement as added evidence.
derived_gate11_requirements.basis: Provenance semiring annotations and view/query determinacy

limits: The papers are formal database-theory sources; their guarantees are conditional on declared models, queries/views, and annotations.
The Gate 11 instrument supports software-level conditional checks only; it makes no human meaning, learning, usability, or causal claim.
